overall: The AG found one violation: the February 1, 2021 minutes inaccurately recorded the chair's public comment response. Other minutes, document-list, public comment, and complaint-review allegations were rejected; unalleged roll call omissions were noted.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the October 7, 2020 retreat minutes were insufficiently detailed and omitted substance for about 15 topics discussed.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the revised minutes adequately capture the substance of the discussions that occurred so that a member of the public who did not attend the meeting could read the minutes and have an understanding of what occurred.

allegations.summary: Complaint that listing the document as 'Open Meeting Law Complaint-Butler' was inaccurate because the Board reviewed only the two-page form, not the full attached pages.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the minutes sufficiently identify the discussions that occurred with respect to the complaints as well as the documents that the Board used during the meetings.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the January 19 and February 1, 2021 minutes failed to include a complainant's public comment statements.
allegations.key_passage: a public body is not required to capture every comment made during public comment in order to substantially comply with the accuracy requirement of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The February 1, 2021 minutes recorded the chair saying all members had received a complaint copy in response to public comment, which the audio did not support.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that this statement in the minutes does not accurately reflect the discussion that occurred.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the Board failed to review the entire multi-page Open Meeting Law complaint, reviewing only the two-page form.
allegations.key_passage: While the Open Meeting Law requires that a public body review a complaint during a meeting, the body’s decision to review only portions of the complaint is the body’s prerogative.

allegations.summary: Not alleged by complainants; the AG noted the December 21, 2020, January 19, and February 1, 2021 minutes recorded unanimous votes without roll call votes by member.
allegations.key_passage: This does not satisfy the Open Meeting Law’s requirement that the vote of each member be recorded by roll call and entered in the minutes.

remedy: Revise the February 1, 2021 minutes to accurately reflect the chair's public comment response and certify to the AG within 30 days.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to revise the February 1, 2021, meeting minutes to accurately reflect the chair’s response provided during the public comment period and to certify to this office within thirty (30) days of the date of this letter that it has done so.
